cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which kind of event or phenomenon can be studied geographically, since the reach of geography is extensive?
cards.back: Thus, the reach of geography is extensive and each and every event or phenomenon which varies over space and time can be studied geographically.
cards.quote: Thus, the reach of geography is extensive and each and every event or phenomenon which varies over space and time can be studied geographically.
reasons: review:Front already gives away 'reach is extensive' and the answer is an open sentence; the mark-carrying idea 'varies over space and time' is not cued, so several answers ('everything', 'all events') fit. Better as a key line with that phrase blanked.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Body-part metaphors used for physical features: name the six.
cards.back:
‘face’ of the earth
‘eye’ of the storm
‘mouth’ of the river
‘snout’ (nose) of the glacier
‘neck’ of the isthmus
‘profile’ of the soil
cards.quote: We often talk of the ‘face’ of the earth, ‘eye’ of the storm, ‘mouth’ of the river, ‘snout’ (nose) of the glacier, ‘neck’ of the isthmus and ‘profile’ of the soil.
reasons: review:Body-part metaphors (face of the earth, eye of the storm...) are illustrative colour from the intro, not exam-tested.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ geographers describe the ‘state/country’ as a ‘____’.
cards.back: German geographers describe the ‘state/country’ as a ‘living organism’.
cards.quote: German geographers describe the ‘state/country’ as a ‘living organism’.
reasons: review:Trivia: German geographers' 'living organism' metaphor is intro colour, not a mark-carrying fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Networks of road, railways and water ways have often been described as “____”.
cards.back: Networks of road, railways and water ways have often been described as “arteries of circulation”.
cards.quote: Networks of road, railways and water ways have often been described as “arteries of circulation”.
reasons: review:Trivia: 'arteries of circulation' metaphor is intro colour, not exam-tested.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the elements of material culture created by human beings.
cards.back:
Houses
villages
cities
road-rail networks
industries
farms
ports
items of our daily use
cards.quote: Houses, villages, cities, road-rail networks, industries, farms, ports, items of our daily use and all other elements of material culture have been created by human beings using the resources provided by the physical environment.
reasons: review:Illustrative examples ('and all other elements of material culture'), not a fixed list worth memorising. | Open-ended 'name the elements': any material-culture item is a valid answer; the 8 listed are only examples.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: While physical environment has been greatly ____ by human beings, it has also, in turn, ____ human lives.
cards.back: While physical environment has been greatly modified by human beings, it has also, in turn, impacted human lives.
cards.quote: While physical environment has been greatly modified by human beings, it has also, in turn, impacted human lives.
reasons: review:Blanks have synonyms: 'modified' (changed/altered), 'impacted' (affected/influenced); no single right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Human geography offers a ____ of the interrelationships between earth and human beings.
cards.back: Human geography offers a new conception of the interrelationships between earth and human beings.
cards.quote: Human geography offers a new conception of the interrelationships between earth and human beings.
reasons: review:'new conception' is a phrase blank with synonyms (new understanding/view); also the Vidal gloss under a highlighted definition, so should be must. | Gloss under a highlighted definition block; should be must.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does human geography study (nature of human geography)?
cards.back: Human geography studies the inter-relationship between the physical environment and sociocultural environment created by human beings through mutual interaction with each other.
cards.quote: Human geography studies the inter-relationship between the physical environment and sociocultural environment created by human beings through mutual interaction with each other.
reasons: review:Front 'What does human geography study...' is near-identical to card def-human-geography-studies, which has a different answer; student cannot tell which is wanted.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Technology indicates the level of ____ of society.
cards.back: Technology indicates the level of cultural development of society.
cards.quote: Technology indicates the level of cultural development of society.
reasons: review:'cultural development' has near-synonyms (development, social/economic development); front gives no way to pick the exact phrase.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Human beings were able to develop technology after they developed better understanding of ____.
cards.back: Human beings were able to develop technology after they developed better understanding of natural laws.
cards.quote: Human beings were able to develop technology after they developed better understanding of natural laws.
reasons: review:'natural laws' vs 'nature' (NCERT's next sentence says 'knowledge about Nature'); not a single right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: You can see that knowledge about Nature is extremely important to develop technology and technology ____ of environment on human beings.
cards.back: You can see that knowledge about Nature is extremely important to develop technology and technology loosens the shackles of environment on human beings.
cards.quote: You can see that knowledge about Nature is extremely important to develop technology and technology loosens the shackles of environment on human beings.
reasons: review:Blank is an idiom ('loosens the shackles'); alternatives (reduces the hold, frees) are equally right, so not a mark-carrying single word.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In the early stages of their interaction with their natural environment humans were ____ by it.
cards.back: In the early stages of their interaction with their natural environment humans were greatly influenced by it.
cards.quote: In the early stages of their interaction with their natural environment humans were greatly influenced by it.
reasons: review:'greatly influenced' vs affected/controlled/dominated; blank is a loose phrase with several valid fills.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is environmental determinism?
cards.back: This type of interaction between primitive human society and strong forces of nature was termed as environmental determinism.
cards.quote: This type of interaction between primitive human society and strong forces of nature was termed as environmental determinism.
reasons: review:Back opens with 'This type of interaction' with no antecedent in the quote, so it does not answer 'What is environmental determinism?' standalone; quote must include the preceding sentence(s).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In NCERT's example of naturalisation of humans, where does Benda live?
cards.back: Benda lives in the wilds of the Abujh Maad area of central India.
cards.quote: Benda lives in the wilds of the Abujh Maad area of central India.

source.section: Naturalisation of Humans and Humanisation of Nature

reasons: review:Case-story filler (Benda's village); location of a fictional character is not exam material.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which primitive form of agriculture does Benda's tribe practise in the penda (forest)?
cards.back: the penda (forest) where his tribe practices a primitive form of agriculture called shifting cultivation
cards.quote: the penda (forest) where his tribe practices a primitive form of agriculture called shifting cultivation

source.section: Naturalisation of Humans and Humanisation of Nature

reasons: review:Case-story filler (Benda story); the concept (shifting cultivation) is not what the card teaches.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: You will realise that in all such cases nature is a powerful force, ____.
cards.back: You will realise that in all such cases nature is a powerful force, worshipped, revered and conserved.
cards.quote: You will realise that in all such cases nature is a powerful force, worshipped, revered and conserved.

source.section: Naturalisation of Humans and Humanisation of Nature

reasons: review:Blank is three adjectives ('worshipped, revered and conserved'); synonyms abound; 'such cases' has no antecedent in the front.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The human activities create ____.
cards.back: The human activities create cultural landscape.
cards.quote: The human activities create cultural landscape.

source.section: Naturalisation of Humans and Humanisation of Nature

reasons: review:Front 'The human activities create ____' is too bare; 'possibilities', 'imprints' also fit the text. Needs context (landscape) or a fuller frame.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the imprints of human activities that form the cultural landscape.
cards.back:
health resorts on highlands
huge urban sprawls
fields, orchards and pastures in plains and rolling hills
ports on the coasts
oceanic routes on the oceanic surface
satellites in the space
cards.quote: The imprints of human activities are created everywhere; health resorts on highlands, huge urban sprawls, fields, orchards and pastures in plains and rolling hills, ports on the coasts, oceanic routes on the oceanic surface and satellites in the space.

source.section: Naturalisation of Humans and Humanisation of Nature

reasons: review:Illustrative examples of imprints (resorts, ports, satellites), not a headed list worth memorising. | Open-ended 'name the imprints': many valid answers beyond the six NCERT examples.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In NCERT's example of humanisation of nature, which town has winters of fierce winds and heavy snow?
cards.back: Winters in the town of Trondheim mean fierce winds and heavy snow.
cards.quote: Winters in the town of Trondheim mean fierce winds and heavy snow.

source.section: Naturalisation of Humans and Humanisation of Nature

reasons: review:Case-story filler (Trondheim); the town name is not exam material.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What has allowed the people of Trondheim and others to overcome the constraints imposed by nature?
cards.back: It is technology that has allowed the people of Trondheim and others to overcome the constraints imposed by nature.
cards.quote: It is technology that has allowed the people of Trondheim and others to overcome the constraints imposed by nature.

source.section: Naturalisation of Humans and Humanisation of Nature

reasons: review:Built on the Trondheim/Kari case story (front names 'the people of Trondheim' which the student cannot see) and duplicates ex-trondheim; the general principle ('technology loosens the shackles of environment', p.2) is the exam-worthy point. Drop or reword without the case.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Table 1.1: the Early Colonial period approach and its broad features.
cards.back:
Exploration and description
Imperial and trade interests prompted the discovery and exploration of new areas. An encyclopaedic description of the area formed an important aspect of the geographer's account.
cards.quote: Imperial and trade interests prompted the discovery and exploration of new areas. An encyclopaedic description of the area formed an important aspect of the geographer's account.

source.section: Table 1.1: Broad Stages and Thrust of Human Geography

reasons: review:Back adds the approach line 'Exploration and description', which is not in the quote; back must equal or be a substring of the quote for kind fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Table 1.1: the Later Colonial period approach and its broad features.
cards.back:
Regional analysis
Elaborate description of all aspects of a region were undertaken. The idea was that all the regions were part of a whole, i.e. (the earth); so, understanding the parts in totality would lead to an understanding of the whole.
cards.quote: Elaborate description of all aspects of a region were undertaken. The idea was that all the regions were part of a whole, i.e. (the earth); so, understanding the parts in totality would lead to an understanding of the whole.

source.section: Table 1.1: Broad Stages and Thrust of Human Geography

reasons: review:Back adds the approach line 'Regional analysis', which is not in the quote; back must equal or be a substring of the quote for kind fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Table 1.1: the 1930s (inter-War period) approach and its broad features.
cards.back:
Areal differentiation
The focus was on identifying the uniqueness of any region and understanding how and why it was different from others.
cards.quote: The focus was on identifying the uniqueness of any region and understanding how and why it was different from others.

source.section: Table 1.1: Broad Stages and Thrust of Human Geography

reasons: review:Back adds the approach line 'Areal differentiation', which is not in the quote; back must equal or be a substring of the quote for kind fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Table 1.1: the late 1950s to late 1960s approach and its broad features.
cards.back:
Spatial organisation
Marked by the use of computers and sophisticated statistical tools. Laws of physics were often applied to map and analyse human phenomena. This phase was called the quantitative revolution.
cards.quote: Marked by the use of computers and sophisticated statistical tools. Laws of physics were often applied to map and analyse human phenomena. This phase was called the quantitative revolution.

source.section: Table 1.1: Broad Stages and Thrust of Human Geography

reasons: review:Back adds the approach line 'Spatial organisation', which is not in the quote; back must equal or be a substring of the quote for kind fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The main objective was to identify ____ for different human activities.
cards.back: The main objective was to identify mappable patterns for different human activities.
cards.quote: The main objective was to identify mappable patterns for different human activities.

source.section: Table 1.1: Broad Stages and Thrust of Human Geography

reasons: review:Front never says which phase (quantitative revolution / spatial organisation); 'main objective' of what? Several readings.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Table 1.1: the 1990s approach and its broad features.
cards.back:
Post-modernism in geography
The grand generalisations and the applicability of universal theories to explain the human conditions were questioned. The importance of understanding each local context in its own right was emphasised.
cards.quote: The grand generalisations and the applicability of universal theories to explain the human conditions were questioned. The importance of understanding each local context in its own right was emphasised.

source.section: Table 1.1: Broad Stages and Thrust of Human Geography

reasons: review:Back adds the approach line 'Post-modernism in geography', which is not in the quote; back must equal or be a substring of the quote for kind fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Table 1.2: which sister discipline does each sub-field of Economic Geography, from Resources to Tourism, interface with?
cards.back:
Geography of Resources: Resource Economics
Geography of Agriculture: Agricultural Sciences
Geography of Industries: Industrial Economics
Geography of Marketing: Business Studies, Economics, Commerce
Geography of Tourism: Tourism and Travel Management
cards.quote: Geography of Resources Resource Economics Geography of Agriculture Agricultural Sciences Geography of Industries Industrial Economics Geography of Marketing Business Studies, Economics, Commerce Geography of Tourism Tourism and Travel Management

source.section: Fields and Sub-fields of Human Geography

reasons: review:Front caps the list 'from Resources to Tourism' although Table 1.2 has six Economic sub-fields (Geography of International Trade / International Trade is left out), so the cut-off is arbitrary and a student who names all six is marked wrong; make it all six or ask for one pair.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The population of the world is ____.
cards.back: The population of the world is unevenly distributed.
cards.quote: The population of the world is unevenly distributed.
reasons: review:Front 'The population of the world is ____' has many valid fills (growing, large, increasing); no single answer.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Region X has an area of 100 sq km and a population of 1,50,000 persons. What is its density?
cards.back: = 1,500 person/sq km
cards.quote: = 1,500 person/sq km
cards.note: Density = population divided by area: 1,50,000 / 100 = 1,500 persons per sq km.
reasons: review:Worked example only; the Density = Population/Area formula is never carded and back is a bare fragment '= 1,500 person/sq km'.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three groups of factors influencing the distribution of population.
cards.back:
I. Geographical Factors
II. Economic Factors
III. Social and Cultural Factors
cards.quote:
I. Geographical Factors
II. Economic Factors
III. Social and Cultural Factors

source.section: Factors Influencing the Distribution of Population

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the four geographical factors influencing the distribution of population.
cards.back:
(i) Availability of water
(ii) Landforms
(iii) Climate
(iv) Soils
cards.quote:
(i) Availability of water
(ii) Landforms
(iii) Climate
(iv) Soils

source.section: Factors Influencing the Distribution of Population

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ is the most important factor for life.
cards.back: Water is the most important factor for life.
cards.quote: Water is the most important factor for life.
reasons: review:Front gives no context; air, food or sunlight equally plausible for 'most important factor for life'.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: People prefer living on ____ and ____.
cards.back: People prefer living on flat plains and gentle slopes.
cards.quote: People prefer living on flat plains and gentle slopes.
reasons: review:Open fill: fertile land, coasts or low-lying areas are also plausible; two multi-word blanks with paraphrase risk.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Areas with very heavy rainfall or extreme and harsh climates have ____.
cards.back: Areas with very heavy rainfall or extreme and harsh climates have low population.
cards.quote: Areas with very heavy rainfall or extreme and harsh climates have low population.
reasons: review:Front does not say what is asked (population vs agriculture vs development); 'low population' is not the only fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ regions were inhabited from early periods in history due to their pleasant climate.
cards.back: Mediterranean regions were inhabited from early periods in history due to their pleasant climate.
cards.quote: Mediterranean regions were inhabited from early periods in history due to their pleasant climate.
reasons: review:Many regions (temperate, coastal, riverine) fit 'inhabited from early periods due to pleasant climate'; only recall of NCERT example resolves it.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which copper belt in Africa is an example of mineral deposits making an area densely populated?
cards.back: So, skilled and semi-skilled workers move to these areas and make them densely populated. Katanga Zambia copper belt in Africa is one such good example.
cards.quote: So, skilled and semi-skilled workers move to these areas and make them densely populated. Katanga Zambia copper belt in Africa is one such good example.
reasons: review:Single-location example (Katanga Zambia copper belt) is case filler; back also opens with dangling 'So,'.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ provide job opportunities and attract large numbers of people.
cards.back: Industrial belts provide job opportunities and attract large numbers of people.
cards.quote: Industrial belts provide job opportunities and attract large numbers of people.
reasons: review:Dangling subject; cities, industries or mining areas also fit 'provide job opportunities and attract large numbers of people'.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which region of Japan is thickly populated because of a number of industries?
cards.back: The Kobe-Osaka region of Japan is thickly populated because of the presence of a number of industries.
cards.quote: The Kobe-Osaka region of Japan is thickly populated because of the presence of a number of industries.
reasons: review:Single-region example (Kobe-Osaka) is case filler; also the quote crosses the page 8/9 break so the automated quote check on pdftotext will fail.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Some places attract more people because they have ____.
cards.back: Some places attract more people because they have religious or cultural significance.
cards.quote: Some places attract more people because they have religious or cultural significance.
reasons: review:Open fill: fertile land, minerals or jobs also attract people; 'religious or cultural significance' not uniquely determined.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Population change in an area is an important indicator of ____, ____ and historical and cultural background of the region.
cards.back: Population change in an area is an important indicator of economic development, social upliftment and historical and cultural background of the region.
cards.quote: Population change in an area is an important indicator of economic development, social upliftment and historical and cultural background of the region.
reasons: review:Two open multi-word blanks (economic development, social upliftment) that students can paraphrase (progress, social change).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is growth of population?
cards.back: Change of population in particular area between two points of time is known as growth of population.
cards.quote: Change of population in particular area between two points of time is known as growth of population.

source.section: Some Basic Concepts of Population Geography

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: By how much did India's population grow between 2001 and 2011, in actual numbers?
cards.back: if we deduct the population of India 2001 (102.70 crore) from population of 2011 (121.02 crore) then we shall get the growth of population (18.15 crores) in actual numbers.
cards.quote: if we deduct the population of India 2001 (102.70 crore) from population of 2011 (121.02 crore) then we shall get the growth of population (18.15 crores) in actual numbers.

source.section: Some Basic Concepts of Population Geography

reasons: review:NCERT figures are internally inconsistent (121.02 - 102.70 = 18.32, not 18.15 crore) and not real census values; trivia that teaches a wrong subtraction; back starts lowercase 'if'.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In the CBR formula, what do CBR, B and P stand for?
cards.back: Here, CBR = Crude Birth Rate; B = live births during the year; P= Estimated mid year population of the area.
cards.quote: Here, CBR = Crude Birth Rate; B = live births during the year; P= Estimated mid year population of the area.
reasons: review:Symbol key for a formula whose formula (CBR = B/P x 1000) is not on any card; useless without the formula card.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In the CDR formula, what do CDR, D and P stand for?
cards.back: Here, CDR=Crude Death Rate; D= Number of deaths; P=Estimated mid-year population of that year.
cards.quote: Here, CDR=Crude Death Rate; D= Number of deaths; P=Estimated mid-year population of that year.
reasons: review:Symbol key for a formula whose formula (CDR = D/P x 1000) is not on any card; useless without the formula card.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Population growth occurs not only by ____ but also due to ____.
cards.back: Population growth occurs not only by increasing births rate but also due to decreasing death rate.
cards.quote: Population growth occurs not only by increasing births rate but also due to decreasing death rate.
reasons: review:Open double blank; 'increasing births rate' / 'decreasing death rate' can be paraphrased (immigration, falling mortality); NCERT's odd 'births rate' not derivable.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: By and large mortality rates are affected by the region's ____, ____ and levels of its economic development.
cards.back: By and large mortality rates are affected by the region's demographic structure, social advancement and levels of its economic development.
cards.quote: By and large mortality rates are affected by the region's demographic structure, social advancement and levels of its economic development.
reasons: review:Open double blank (demographic structure, social advancement); health facilities, nutrition etc. are equally valid.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Migration may be interpreted as a ____ to achieve a ____ between population and resources.
cards.back: Migration may be interpreted as a spontaneous effort to achieve a better balance between population and resources.
cards.quote: Migration may be interpreted as a spontaneous effort to achieve a better balance between population and resources.
reasons: review:Blanks 'spontaneous effort', 'better balance' are paraphrasable (natural attempt, good balance); no single fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: People migrate for a ____.
cards.back: People migrate for a better economic and social life.
cards.quote: People migrate for a better economic and social life.
reasons: review:Open fill: many reasons people migrate (jobs, education, safety); only recall of NCERT phrase resolves it.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The theory tells us that population of any region changes from ____ to ____
cards.back: The theory tells us that population of any region changes from high births and high deaths to low births and low deaths
cards.quote: The theory tells us that population of any region changes from high births and high deaths to low births and low deaths
reasons: review:Front says 'The theory' without naming demographic transition; blanks are long paraphrasable phrases (high growth to low growth).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In demographic transition theory, what are the stages of change in population collectively known as?
cards.back: The theory tells us that population of any region changes from high births and high deaths to low births and low deaths as society progresses from rural agrarian and illiterate to urban industrial and literate society. These changes occur in stages which are collectively known as the demographic cycle.
cards.quote: The theory tells us that population of any region changes from high births and high deaths to low births and low deaths as society progresses from rural agrarian and illiterate to urban industrial and literate society. These changes occur in stages which are collectively known as the demographic cycle.
reasons: review:Front says 'demographic transition theory ... stages ... collectively known as' so 'demographic transition' is an equally natural answer; the NCERT term 'demographic cycle' is not uniquely cued. Make it a term card with the sentence and 'demographic cycle' blanked.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Improvements in ____ lead to decline in mortality. Because of this gap the ____ to population is high.
cards.back: Improvements in sanitation and health conditions lead to decline in mortality. Because of this gap the net addition to population is high.
cards.quote: Improvements in sanitation and health conditions lead to decline in mortality. Because of this gap the net addition to population is high.
reasons: review:Front omits what the 'gap' is (fertility-mortality gap) and joins two sentences with two blanks; 'net addition' vs 'natural increase' ambiguous.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In the last stage of demographic transition, what does deliberate control of family size show about human beings?
cards.back: The population becomes urbanised, literate and has high technical know- how and deliberately controls the family size. This shows that human beings are extremely flexible and are able to adjust their fertility.
cards.quote: The population becomes urbanised, literate and has high technical know- how and deliberately controls the family size. This shows that human beings are extremely flexible and are able to adjust their fertility.
reasons: review:Open 'what does it show' inference line with no single mark-carrying word (flexible / adaptable / able to adjust fertility all fit); low-yield, the testable content is the stage-3 features, already on fact-stage-3-features.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: At what stages of demographic transition are countries in the present day?
cards.back: In the present day, different countries are at different stages of demographic transition.
cards.quote: In the present day, different countries are at different stages of demographic transition.
reasons: review:Front 'at what stages?' has no single answer (back is 'different stages'); filler line, not examinable.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Access to family planning services is a significant factor in ____ and improving ____.
cards.back: Access to family planning services is a significant factor in limiting population growth and improving women's health.
cards.quote: Access to family planning services is a significant factor in limiting population growth and improving women's health.
reasons: review:Open double blank (limiting population growth, women's health); reducing birth rate etc. are equally valid.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name some measures which can help population control.
cards.back: Propaganda, free availability of contraceptives and tax disincentives for large families are some of the measures which can help population control.
cards.quote: Propaganda, free availability of contraceptives and tax disincentives for large families are some of the measures which can help population control.
reasons: review:Front says 'some measures', so any measure a student names (education, late marriage) is right; NCERT lists exactly three.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Any further increase would result in a population crash caused by ____.
cards.back: Any further increase would result in a population crash caused by famine, disease and war.
cards.quote: Any further increase would result in a population crash caused by famine, disease and war.
reasons: review:Dangling 'Any further increase' and no mention of Malthus; three-item blank paraphrasable (famine and epidemics).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The ____ checks are better than the ____ checks.
cards.back: The preventive checks are better than the physical checks.
cards.quote: The preventive checks are better than the physical checks.
reasons: review:Malthus's standard terms are preventive vs positive checks; NCERT's 'physical' is non-derivable and blank order is swappable; front lacks Malthus context.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Migrants who move out of a place are called ____.
cards.back: Migrants who move out of a place are called Emigrants.
cards.quote: Migrants who move out of a place are called Emigrants.
reasons: review:Duplicates def-emigration (same NCERT sentence); no extra value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Define growth (as different from development).
cards.back: The difference is that growth is quantitative and value neutral. It may have a positive or a negative sign.
cards.quote: The difference is that growth is quantitative and value neutral. It may have a positive or a negative sign.
cards.note: Growth can be an increase or a decrease; it only counts change in quantity.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Define development.
cards.back: Development means a qualitative change which is always value positive.
cards.quote: Development means a qualitative change which is always value positive.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Development occurs when there is a positive change in ____.
cards.back: Development occurs when there is a positive change in quality.
cards.quote: Development occurs when there is a positive change in quality.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: development cannot take place unless there is an ____ or addition to the existing conditions.
cards.back: development cannot take place unless there is an increment or addition to the existing conditions.
cards.quote: development cannot take place unless there is an increment or addition to the existing conditions.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Does positive growth always lead to development?
cards.back: Development occurs when positive growth takes place. Yet, positive growth does not always lead to development.
cards.quote: Development occurs when positive growth takes place. Yet, positive growth does not always lead to development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: NCERT example: a city's population grows from one lakh to two lakhs. What do we say about the city?
cards.back: if the population of a city grows from one lakh to two lakhs over a period of time, we say the city has grown.
cards.quote: if the population of a city grows from one lakh to two lakhs over a period of time, we say the city has grown.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: NCERT example: a city doubles in population but housing, basic services and other characteristics stay the same. What follows?
cards.back: other characteristics remain the same, then this growth has not been accompanied by development.
cards.quote: other characteristics remain the same, then this growth has not been accompanied by development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ are central to all development under this concept.
cards.back: People are central to all development under this concept.
cards.quote: People are central to all development under this concept.
reasons: review:'this concept' is a dangling reference (human development not named); 'People' could be Humans/Individuals.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In Dr Haq's concept of human development, what is true of the choices people have over time?
cards.back:
They are not fixed
These choices are not fixed but keep on changing.
cards.quote: These choices are not fixed but keep on changing.
reasons: review:Front 'what is true of the choices people have over time' is vague: a student could equally answer 'they are enlarged by development'; only the NCERT sentence says 'not fixed, keep changing'. Low value on its own.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: According to him, development is all about enlarging people's ____ in order to lead long, healthy lives with dignity.
cards.back: According to him, development is all about enlarging people's choices in order to lead long, healthy lives with dignity.
cards.quote: According to him, development is all about enlarging people's choices in order to lead long, healthy lives with dignity.
reasons: review:'According to him' has no antecedent on the front; card cannot stand alone.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: NCERT example: why can an uneducated child not choose to become a doctor?
cards.back: an uneducated child cannot make the choice to be a doctor because her choice has got limited by her lack of education.
cards.quote: an uneducated child cannot make the choice to be a doctor because her choice has got limited by her lack of education.
reasons: review:Case-story filler: restates NCERT's illustrative example; the concept (capabilities limit choices) is on card 22.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The opportunities available to people must be equal irrespective of their ____, ____, income and in the Indian case, ____.
cards.back: The opportunities available to people must be equal irrespective of their gender, race, income and in the Indian case, caste.
cards.quote: The opportunities available to people must be equal irrespective of their gender, race, income and in the Indian case, caste.

source.section: The Four Pillars of Human Development

reasons: review:Three blanks with interchangeable order (gender/race) and other plausible fills (religion); not one right answer.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which groups in India drop out of school in large numbers, showing how choices get limited?
cards.back: In India, a large number of women and persons belonging to socially and economically backward groups drop out of school.
cards.quote: In India, a large number of women and persons belonging to socially and economically backward groups drop out of school.

source.section: The Four Pillars of Human Development

reasons: review:Illustration of equity (school dropouts), low standalone exam value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: All ____, ____ and ____ resources must be used keeping in mind the future.
cards.back: All environmental, financial and human resources must be used keeping in mind the future.
cards.quote: All environmental, financial and human resources must be used keeping in mind the future.

source.section: The Four Pillars of Human Development

reasons: review:Three blanks (environmental, financial, human) in interchangeable order; not one right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: People are not participants in development but only ____.
cards.back: People are not participants in development but only passive recipients.
cards.quote: People are not participants in development but only passive recipients.
reasons: review:Front does not name the welfare approach; 'passive recipients' has synonyms (beneficiaries, recipients).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The question of human choices is ____ and the emphasis is on the provision of basic needs of defined sections.
cards.back: The question of human choices is ignored and the emphasis is on the provision of basic needs of defined sections.
cards.quote: The question of human choices is ignored and the emphasis is on the provision of basic needs of defined sections.
reasons: review:Front does not name the basic needs approach; 'ignored' has synonyms (neglected, overlooked).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The closer a score is to one, the ____ is the level of human development.
cards.back: The closer a score is to one, the greater is the level of human development.
cards.quote: The closer a score is to one, the greater is the level of human development.
reasons: review:Blank 'greater' has a synonym 'higher'; not one right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How does NCERT describe HDI scores of 0.983 and 0.268?
cards.back: Therefore, a score of 0.983 would be considered very high while 0.268 would mean a very low level of human development.
cards.quote: Therefore, a score of 0.983 would be considered very high while 0.268 would mean a very low level of human development.
reasons: review:Trivia: NCERT's sample scores 0.983 and 0.268; the rule (closer to 1 = higher) is card 51.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The human development index measures ____ in human development.
cards.back: The human development index measures attainments in human development.
cards.quote: The human development index measures attainments in human development.
reasons: review:Blank 'attainments' has synonyms (achievements, progress); not one right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does the human poverty index take into account to show the shortfall in human development?
cards.back:
the probability of not surviving till the age of 40
the adult illiteracy rate
the number of people who do not have access to clean water
the number of small children who are underweight
cards.quote: The probability of not surviving till the age of 40, the adult illiteracy rate, the number of people who do not have access to clean water, and the number of small children who are underweight are all taken into account to show the shortfall in human development in any region.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Often the human poverty index is ____ than the human development index.
cards.back: Often the human poverty index is more revealing than the human development index.
cards.quote: Often the human poverty index is more revealing than the human development index.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Looking at both these measures of human development together gives an ____ of the human development situation in a country.
cards.back: Looking at both these measures of human development together gives an accurate picture of the human development situation in a country.
cards.quote: Looking at both these measures of human development together gives an accurate picture of the human development situation in a country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which body has published the Human Development Report every year since 1990?
cards.back: Since 1990, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has been publishing the Human Development Report every year.
cards.quote: Since 1990, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has been publishing the Human Development Report every year.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does the Human Development Report provide?
cards.back: This report provides a rank-wise list of all member countries according to the level of human development.
cards.quote: This report provides a rank-wise list of all member countries according to the level of human development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the two important indices used by the UNDP to measure human development.
cards.back: The Human Development index and the Human Poverty index are two important indices to measure human development used by the UNDP.
cards.quote: The Human Development index and the Human Poverty index are two important indices to measure human development used by the UNDP.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which country officially proclaims Gross National Happiness (GNH) as the measure of its progress?
cards.back: Bhutan is the only country in the world to officially proclaim the Gross National Happiness (GNH) as the measure of the country's progress.
cards.quote: Bhutan is the only country in the world to officially proclaim the Gross National Happiness (GNH) as the measure of the country's progress.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: GNH encourages us to think of the ____, non-material and ____ aspects of development.
cards.back: GNH encourages us to think of the spiritual, non-material and qualitative aspects of development.
cards.quote: GNH encourages us to think of the spiritual, non-material and qualitative aspects of development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Size of the territory and ____ are not directly related to human development.
cards.back: Size of the territory and per capita income are not directly related to human development.
cards.quote: Size of the territory and per capita income are not directly related to human development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Often ____ countries have done better than larger ones in human development.
cards.back: Often smaller countries have done better than larger ones in human development.
cards.quote: Often smaller countries have done better than larger ones in human development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: NCERT example: which countries rank higher than India on the HDI despite smaller economies?
cards.back: For example, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago have a higher rank than India in the human development index despite having smaller economies.
cards.quote: For example, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago have a higher rank than India in the human development index despite having smaller economies.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: NCERT example: which Indian state does better than Punjab and Gujarat in human development despite lower per capita income?
cards.back: Similarly, within India, Kerala performs much better than Punjab and Gujarat in human development despite having lower per capita income.
cards.quote: Similarly, within India, Kerala performs much better than Punjab and Gujarat in human development despite having lower per capita income.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How are countries classified on the basis of the human development index?
cards.back: Countries can be classified into four groups on the basis of the human development scores earned by them (Table 3.2).
cards.quote: Countries can be classified into four groups on the basis of the human development scores earned by them (Table 3.2).
cards.note: Table 3.2: Very High above 0.800; High 0.700-0.799; Medium 0.550-0.699; Low below 0.550.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What HDI score marks a country as having very high human development?
cards.back: Countries with very high human development index are those which have a score of over 0.800.
cards.quote: Countries with very high human development index are those which have a score of over 0.800.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many countries does the very high human development group include (Human Development Report 2025)?
cards.back: According to the Human Development Report of 2025, this group includes 74 countries.
cards.quote: According to the Human Development Report of 2025, this group includes 74 countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many countries are in the high level of human development group?
cards.back: High level of human development group has 50 countries.
cards.quote: High level of human development group has 50 countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which human development group is the largest, and how many countries does it have?
cards.back: Countries with medium levels of human development form the largest group. There are 53 countries in the medium level of human development.
cards.quote: Countries with medium levels of human development form the largest group. There are 53 countries in the medium level of human development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many countries record low levels of human development?
cards.back: As many as 26 countries record low levels of human development.
cards.quote: As many as 26 countries record low levels of human development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In Table 3.2, an HDI score of what level puts a country in the Low category?
cards.back: Low below 0.550
cards.quote: Low below 0.550

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Most countries in the medium human development group emerged in which period?
cards.back: Most of these are countries which have emerged in the period after the Second World War.
cards.quote: Most of these are countries which have emerged in the period after the Second World War.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the origins of many countries in the medium human development group?
cards.back: Some countries from this group were former colonies while many others have emerged after the break up of the erstwhile Soviet Union in 1990.
cards.quote: Some countries from this group were former colonies while many others have emerged after the break up of the erstwhile Soviet Union in 1990.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Many of these countries have been rapidly improving their human development score by adopting more ____ and reducing social discrimination.
cards.back: Many of these countries have been rapidly improving their human development score by adopting more people-oriented policies and reducing social discrimination.
cards.quote: Many of these countries have been rapidly improving their human development score by adopting more people-oriented policies and reducing social discrimination.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Countries with higher human development are those where a lot of investment in the ____ has taken place.
cards.back: Countries with higher human development are those where a lot of investment in the social sector has taken place.
cards.quote: Countries with higher human development are those where a lot of investment in the social sector has taken place.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Altogether, a higher investment in people and ____ has set this group of countries apart from the others.
cards.back: Altogether, a higher investment in people and good governance has set this group of countries apart from the others.
cards.quote: Altogether, a higher investment in people and good governance has set this group of countries apart from the others.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What do many countries with a high human development score have in common historically?
cards.back: You will notice that many of these countries have been the former imperial powers.
cards.quote: You will notice that many of these countries have been the former imperial powers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where are many countries with a high human development score located?
cards.back: Many of the countries with a high human development score are located in Europe and represent the industrialised western world.
cards.quote: Many of the countries with a high human development score are located in Europe and represent the industrialised western world.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Human Development Report 2025: what is India's rank?
cards.back: India ranks 130 out of 193 countries, from 133 in 2022.
cards.quote: India ranks 130 out of 193 countries, from 133 in 2022.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Human Development Report 2025: how did India's HDI value change from 2022 to 2023?
cards.back: It registered an HDI value increase to 0.685 in 2023 from 0.676 in 2022.
cards.quote: It registered an HDI value increase to 0.685 in 2023 from 0.676 in 2022.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What situation are many small countries with low human development going through?
cards.back: A large proportion of these are small countries which have been going through political turmoil and social instability in the form of civil war, famine or a high incidence of diseases.
cards.quote: A large proportion of these are small countries which have been going through political turmoil and social instability in the form of civil war, famine or a high incidence of diseases.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Is it right to blame low human development on the religion or community of the people?
cards.back: For example, X country has lower human development because its people follow Y religion, or belong to Z community. Such statements are misleading.
cards.quote: For example, X country has lower human development because its people follow Y religion, or belong to Z community. Such statements are misleading.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: To understand why a region reports low or high human development, what pattern should we look at?
cards.back: To understand why a particular region keeps reporting low or high levels of human development it is important to look at the pattern of government expenditure on the social sector.
cards.quote: To understand why a particular region keeps reporting low or high levels of human development it is important to look at the pattern of government expenditure on the social sector.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Countries with high levels of human development invest more in the ____ and are generally free from political turmoil and instability.
cards.back: Countries with high levels of human development invest more in the social sectors and are generally free from political turmoil and instability.
cards.quote: Countries with high levels of human development invest more in the social sectors and are generally free from political turmoil and instability.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Distribution of the country's resources is also far more ____.
cards.back: Distribution of the country's resources is also far more equitable.
cards.quote: Distribution of the country's resources is also far more equitable.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: On the other hand, places with low levels of human development tend to spend more on ____ rather than social sectors.
cards.back: On the other hand, places with low levels of human development tend to spend more on defence rather than social sectors.
cards.quote: On the other hand, places with low levels of human development tend to spend more on defence rather than social sectors.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Gathering is practised in regions with ____.
cards.back: Gathering is practised in regions with harsh climatic conditions.
cards.quote: Gathering is practised in regions with harsh climatic conditions.
reasons: review:Open phrase blank with no cue: 'regions with ____' could be filled many ways; only the exact NCERT phrase scores.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What do leaves, nuts and tree trunks supply in commercial gathering?
cards.back: leaves supply materials for beverages, drugs, cosmetics, fibres, thatch and fabrics; nuts for food and oils and tree trunk yield rubber, balata, gums and resins.
cards.quote: leaves supply materials for beverages, drugs, cosmetics, fibres, thatch and fabrics; nuts for food and oils and tree trunk yield rubber, balata, gums and resins.
reasons: review:Long list of plant-product uses (beverages, drugs, balata, resins); detail, not exam-tested.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Gathering has little chance of becoming important at the ____ level.
cards.back: Gathering has little chance of becoming important at the global level.
cards.quote: Gathering has little chance of becoming important at the global level.
reasons: review:'at the ____ level' accepts global, international, world; the blank has more than one natural fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which territory does each nomadic community occupy?
cards.back: Each nomadic community occupies a well-identified territory as a matter of tradition.
cards.quote: Each nomadic community occupies a well-identified territory as a matter of tradition.
reasons: review:'Which territory' implies a named place; the answer is only 'a well-identified territory as a matter of tradition', so the front does not lead to one clear answer. Trivia: tradition-bound territory of each community; not a mark-carrying point.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is factory farming?
cards.back: In addition to market gardening, a modern development in the industrial regions of Western Europe and North America is factory farming.
cards.quote: In addition to market gardening, a modern development in the industrial regions of Western Europe and North America is factory farming.
reasons: review:Front asks what factory farming is but back only says it is a modern development in Western Europe and North America; the actual definition (livestock reared in stalls and pens, fed manufactured feedstuff) is the next sentence, so the card teaches no meaning.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How is the discovery of minerals reflected in the history of human development?
cards.back: The discovery of minerals in the history of human development, is reflected in many stages in terms of copper age, bronze age and iron age.
cards.quote: The discovery of minerals in the history of human development, is reflected in many stages in terms of copper age, bronze age and iron age.
reasons: review:Copper, bronze and iron age remark is background story, not a CUET point.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which countries have over fifty per cent of their earnings from minerals alone?
cards.back: Several countries of Africa and few of south America and Asia have over fifty per cent of the earnings from minerals alone.
cards.quote: Several countries of Africa and few of south America and Asia have over fifty per cent of the earnings from minerals alone.
reasons: review:Vague (several countries of Africa, few of South America and Asia); no checkable answer, low exam value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Most of the ____ countries still `manufacture' in the literal sense of the term.
cards.back: Most of the Third World countries still `manufacture' in the literal sense of the term.
cards.quote: Most of the Third World countries still `manufacture' in the literal sense of the term.
reasons: review:Blank "Third World" has many plausible fills (developing, poor, less developed) and is dated trivia, not a mark-carrying fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: But there are many secondary activities which are not carried on in factories such as what is now called the `____' and Tourism industry, etc.
cards.back: But there are many secondary activities which are not carried on in factories such as what is now called the `entertainment industry' and Tourism industry, etc.
cards.quote: But there are many secondary activities which are not carried on in factories such as what is now called the `entertainment industry' and Tourism industry, etc.
reasons: review:Blank has many plausible fills (film, media, IT) and is a passing aside, not an exam fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Automatic factories with feedback and ____ where machines are developed to `think', have sprung up all over the world.
cards.back: Automatic factories with feedback and closed-loop computer control systems where machines are developed to `think', have sprung up all over the world.
cards.quote: Automatic factories with feedback and closed-loop computer control systems where machines are developed to `think', have sprung up all over the world.
reasons: review:Long multi-word blank with no single guessable fill; passing description, low exam value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Modern manufacturing is characterised by a complex ____ and extreme specialisation and ____ for producing more goods with less efforts and low costs.
cards.back: Modern manufacturing is characterised by a complex machine technology and extreme specialisation and division of labour for producing more goods with less efforts and low costs.
cards.quote: Modern manufacturing is characterised by a complex machine technology and extreme specialisation and division of labour for producing more goods with less efforts and low costs.
reasons: review:Two multi-word blanks (machine technology, division of labour) are not uniquely recoverable from the front.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Compare 2.5 sq km of the American corn belt with the same area under factories.
cards.back: For example, 2.5 sq km of the American corn belt usually includes about four large farms employing about 10-20 workers supporting 50-100 persons. But this same area could contain several large integrated factories and employ thousands of workers.
cards.quote: For example, 2.5 sq km of the American corn belt usually includes about four large farms employing about 10-20 workers supporting 50-100 persons. But this same area could contain several large integrated factories and employ thousands of workers.
reasons: review:Case-story filler (corn-belt farm vs factory head-counts); not a memory item.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Industries maximise profits by ____. Therefore, industries should be located at points where the production costs are ____.
cards.back: Industries maximise profits by reducing costs. Therefore, industries should be located at points where the production costs are minimum.
cards.quote: Industries maximise profits by reducing costs. Therefore, industries should be located at points where the production costs are minimum.

source.section: Why do Large-scale Industries choose different locations?

reasons: review:Second blank "minimum" equally filled by lowest/least; two blanks.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ is a vital factor for the industry to be located closer to the source of the raw material.
cards.back: Perishability is a vital factor for the industry to be located closer to the source of the raw material.
cards.quote: Perishability is a vital factor for the industry to be located closer to the source of the raw material.
reasons: review:Blank is not unique from the front: bulkiness, weight loss or cost fit equally; only the following sentence disambiguates.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ are processed close to the sources of farm produce or milk supply respectively.
cards.back: Agro-processing and dairy products are processed close to the sources of farm produce or milk supply respectively.
cards.quote: Agro-processing and dairy products are processed close to the sources of farm produce or milk supply respectively.
reasons: review:Blank wording (agro-processing / agro products / perishables) is not unique.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Increasing ____ of industrial processes have reduced the dependence of industry upon the labours.
cards.back: Increasing mechanisation, automation and flexibility of industrial processes have reduced the dependence of industry upon the labours.
cards.quote: Increasing mechanisation, automation and flexibility of industrial processes have reduced the dependence of industry upon the labours.
reasons: review:Three-term blank (mechanisation, automation and flexibility) is not uniquely recoverable; technology/automation also fit.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Industries which use more power are located close to the source of the energy supply such as the ____ industry.
cards.back: Industries which use more power are located close to the source of the energy supply such as the aluminium industry.
cards.quote: Industries which use more power are located close to the source of the energy supply such as the aluminium industry.
reasons: review:Other power-hungry industries (steel, fertiliser) fit the front; example is not unique.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The amount of ____, ____ and ____ determine the size of industry.
cards.back: The amount of capital invested, number of workers employed and volume of production determine the size of industry.
cards.quote: The amount of capital invested, number of workers employed and volume of production determine the size of industry.
reasons: review:Three adjacent multi-word blanks; order and wording ambiguous (amount of ____ applies to only the first).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Capital and transportation do not wield much influence as this type of manufacturing has ____ and most of the tools are devised locally.
cards.back: Capital and transportation do not wield much influence as this type of manufacturing has low commercial significance and most of the tools are devised locally.
cards.quote: Capital and transportation do not wield much influence as this type of manufacturing has low commercial significance and most of the tools are devised locally.
reasons: review:Blank "low commercial significance" is open (limited/little importance); not uniquely recoverable.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What everyday products does household or cottage manufacturing produce?
cards.back: Some common everyday products produced in this sector of manufacturing include foodstuffs, fabrics, mats, containers, tools, furniture, shoes, and figurines from wood lot and forest, shoes, thongs and other articles from leather; pottery and bricks from clays and stones.
cards.quote: Some common everyday products produced in this sector of manufacturing include foodstuffs, fabrics, mats, containers, tools, furniture, shoes, and figurines from wood lot and forest, shoes, thongs and other articles from leather; pottery and bricks from clays and stones.
reasons: review:Laundry list of everyday products with no discriminating fact; not a memory item.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Agro processing includes ____, producing cream, fruit processing and ____.
cards.back: Agro processing includes canning, producing cream, fruit processing and confectionery.
cards.quote: Agro processing includes canning, producing cream, fruit processing and confectionery.
reasons: review:Two open blanks (canning, confectionery) have many plausible fills; low-value list fragment.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the preserving techniques that NCERT says have been known since ancient times.
cards.back:
drying
fermenting
pickling
cards.quote: While some preserving techniques, such as drying, fermenting and pickling, have been known since ancient times
reasons: review:NCERT says 'some preserving techniques, such as drying, fermenting and pickling': a non-exhaustive example list, so 'name the techniques' has other valid answers (salting, smoking); also trivia about pre-Industrial-Revolution use; 'NCERT says' in the front is odd for a student card.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____, plastic, etc. are other examples of chemical based industries.
cards.back: Synthetic fibre, plastic, etc. are other examples of chemical based industries.
cards.quote: Synthetic fibre, plastic, etc. are other examples of chemical based industries.
reasons: review:Blank "Synthetic fibre" not unique (fertiliser, paint, pharmaceutical fit); trivia.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What kind of buildings, rather than massive assembly structures and factories, mark the high-tech industrial landscape?
cards.back:
Neatly spaced, low, modern, dispersed office-plant-lab buildings
Neatly spaced, low, modern, dispersed, office-plant-lab buildings rather than massive assembly structures, factories and storage areas mark the high-tech industrial landscape.
cards.quote: Neatly spaced, low, modern, dispersed, office-plant-lab buildings rather than massive assembly structures, factories and storage areas mark the high-tech industrial landscape.
reasons: review:Answer is a string of five adjectives (neatly spaced, low, modern, dispersed) that the front gives no way to pin down; only 'office-plant-lab' is distinctive. Descriptive landscape detail, low value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name some examples of tertiary activities (workers).
cards.back:
plumber
electrician
technician
launderer
barber
shopkeeper
driver
cashier
teacher
doctor
lawyer
publisher
cards.quote: Common examples are the work of a plumber, electrician, technician, launderer, barber, shopkeeper, driver, cashier, teacher, doctor, lawyer and publisher etc.
reasons: review:Open-ended 'Name some examples' of worker types: any correct job qualifies, so no single right answer; a twelve-job list is low-value recall, not a CUET point.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the tertiary activities discussed in the chapter.
cards.back:
trade
transport
communication
services
cards.quote: Thus, trade, transport, communication and services are some of the tertiary activities discussed in this section.
reasons: review:Front says 'tertiary activities discussed in the chapter' but NCERT's line says 'some of' the activities in this section; tourism and medical tourism are also tertiary and discussed later, so trade/transport/communication/services is not the one right answer. Reword to 'the four activities used to c

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What type of trading centres are rural marketing centres?
cards.back: They serve as trading centres of the most rudimentary type.
cards.quote: They serve as trading centres of the most rudimentary type.
reasons: review:Ambiguous with kl-rural-marketing-quasi-urban: 'What type of trading centres are rural marketing centres?' is equally answered by 'quasi-urban' (previous NCERT sentence) or 'most rudimentary type'. Near-duplicate of that card.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Urban marketing centres have more widely ____ urban services.
cards.back: Urban marketing centres have more widely specialised urban services.
cards.quote: Urban marketing centres have more widely specialised urban services.
reasons: review:Blank 'widely ____ urban services' has several natural fills (developed, distributed, available); only 'specialised' carries NCERT's meaning but the front does not force it.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the professionals whose services are available in urban marketing centres.
cards.back:
teachers
lawyers
consultants
physicians
dentists
veterinary doctors
cards.quote: Services of educational institutions and professionals such as teachers, lawyers, consultants, physicians, dentists and veterinary doctors are available.
reasons: review:List of six professions in urban centres (teachers, lawyers, consultants, physicians, dentists, veterinary doctors) is illustrative filler, not a definition or headed classification.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What can chain stores employ and experiment with?
