cards.front: What per cent of India's population is urban, which NCERT calls quite low but fast-growing?
cards.back:
31.16 per cent
the proportion of urban population (31.16 per cent) in India is quite low but it is showing a much faster rate of growth over the decades.
cards.quote: the proportion of urban population (31.16 per cent) in India is quite low but it is showing a much faster rate of growth over the decades.
reasons: review:Time-bound census statistic (2011); and the front gives no year, so the figure is not the single right answer.

cards.subject: geography
cards.unit: Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition
cards.front: Name industrial areas where rural-urban migration is conspicuous.
cards.back: The rural-urban migration is conspicuous in the case of urban areas along the main road links and railroads in the North Indian Plains, the industrial areas around Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru - Mysuru, Madurai - Coimbatore, Ahmedabad - Surat, Delhi - Kanpur and Ludhiana - Jalandhar.
cards.quote: The rural-urban migration is conspicuous in the case of urban areas along the main road links and railroads in the North Indian Plains, the industrial areas around Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru - Mysuru, Madurai - Coimbatore, Ahmedabad - Surat, Delhi - Kanpur and Ludhiana - Jalandhar.
reasons: review:Long list of seven city-pair industrial belts; low exam value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.unit: Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition
cards.front: Religion is one of the most dominant forces affecting the ____ of the majority of Indians.
cards.back: Religion is one of the most dominant forces affecting the cultural and political life of the majority of Indians.
cards.quote: Religion is one of the most dominant forces affecting the cultural and political life of the majority of Indians.
reasons: review:Generic statement; many valid fills. Blank "cultural and political life" has many acceptable fills (lives, culture, society).

cards.subject: geography
cards.unit: Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition
cards.front: Main worker vs marginal worker: the difference on days worked in a year
cards.back:
Main Worker is a person who works for atleast 183 days ( or six months) in a year.
Marginal Worker is a person who works for less than 183 days ( or six months) in a year.
cards.quote: Main Worker is a person who works for atleast 183 days ( or six months) in a year. Marginal Worker is a person who works for less than 183 days ( or six months) in a year.
reasons: review:Redundant with cards 72 and 73; not an NCERT comparison table so kind difference is misused.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: For this purpose, people may erect houses and other structures and command some area or territory as their ____.
cards.back: For this purpose, people may erect houses and other structures and command some area or territory as their economic support-base.
cards.quote: For this purpose, people may erect houses and other structures and command some area or territory as their economic support-base.
reasons: review:Background elaboration, low exam value; blank 'economic support-base' has a natural rival fill 'resource base' (used in the next sentence).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How far do settlements range in size, according to NCERT?
cards.back: Settlements vary in size and type. They range from a hamlet to metropolitan cities.
cards.quote: Settlements vary in size and type. They range from a hamlet to metropolitan cities.
reasons: review:Generic range statement (hamlet to metropolitan cities); trivia, not a tested point.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: With size, the economic character and social structure of settlements changes and so do its ____ and ____.
cards.back: With size, the economic character and social structure of settlements changes and so do its ecology and technology.
cards.quote: With size, the economic character and social structure of settlements changes and so do its ecology and technology.
reasons: review:Blanks 'ecology' and 'technology' are guessable alternatives (culture, environment, economy); background sentence, low exam value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Cities act as ____ of economic growth
cards.back: Cities act as nodes of economic growth
cards.quote: Cities act as nodes of economic growth
reasons: review:Blank "nodes" has synonyms (centres, hubs, engines, drivers); not a single right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Semi-clustered or fragmented settlements may result from tendency of ____ in a restricted area of ____ settlement.
cards.back: Semi-clustered or fragmented settlements may result from tendency of clustering in a restricted area of dispersed settlement.
cards.quote: Semi-clustered or fragmented settlements may result from tendency of clustering in a restricted area of dispersed settlement.
reasons: review:'clustering' and 'dispersed' have close synonyms (concentration, scattered); blanks not one-answer.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: More often such a pattern may also result from ____ or ____ of a large compact village.
cards.back: More often such a pattern may also result from segregation or fragmentation of a large compact village.
cards.quote: More often such a pattern may also result from segregation or fragmentation of a large compact village.
reasons: review:'segregation or fragmentation' are interchangeable synonyms (division, separation, splitting); order-dependent blanks.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In this type of village the general living area is ____ and ____ from the surrounding farms, barns and pastures.
cards.back: In this type of village the general living area is distinct and separated from the surrounding farms, barns and pastures.
cards.quote: In this type of village the general living area is distinct and separated from the surrounding farms, barns and pastures.
reasons: review:'distinct and separated' are near-synonyms (apart, detached, isolated); blanks not one-answer.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What form does the dispersed or isolated settlement pattern take in India?
cards.back: Dispersed or isolated settlement pattern in India appears in the form of isolated huts or hamlets of few huts in remote jungles
cards.quote: Dispersed or isolated settlement pattern in India appears in the form of isolated huts or hamlets of few huts in remote jungles
reasons: review:Back is cut mid-sentence at the page break: NCERT continues 'or on small hills with farms or pasture on the slopes'. Card omits half of the form of dispersed settlement; quote should span both pages.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Extreme dispersion of settlement is often caused by extremely ____ nature of the ____ and land resource base of habitable areas.
cards.back: Extreme dispersion of settlement is often caused by extremely fragmented nature of the terrain and land resource base of habitable areas.
cards.quote: Extreme dispersion of settlement is often caused by extremely fragmented nature of the terrain and land resource base of habitable areas.
reasons: review:'extremely ____ nature of the ____': rugged/hilly/broken and terrain/land/relief all fit; blanks not one-answer.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Unlike rural settlements, urban settlements are generally ____ and larger in size.
cards.back: Unlike rural settlements, urban settlements are generally compact and larger in size.
cards.quote: Unlike rural settlements, urban settlements are generally compact and larger in size.
reasons: review:Blank "compact" has synonyms (dense, concentrated, nucleated); not a single right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: But the growth rate of urbanisation has ____ during last two decades.
cards.back: But the growth rate of urbanisation has slowed down during last two decades.
cards.quote: But the growth rate of urbanisation has slowed down during last two decades.
reasons: review:'slowed down' has synonyms (declined, decreased, fallen); blank not one-answer.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the first six classes in NCERT's functional classification of Indian towns and cities.
cards.back:
Administrative towns and cities
Industrial towns
Transport Cities
Commercial towns
Mining towns
Garrisson Cantonment towns
cards.quote: On the basis of dominant or specialised functions, Indian cities and towns can be broadly classified as follows: Administrative towns and cities Towns supporting administrative headquarters of higher order are administrative towns, such as Chandigarh, New Delhi, Bhopal, Shillong, Guwahati, Imphal, Srinagar, Gandhinagar, Jaipur, Chennai, etc. Industrial towns Industries constitute prime motive force of these cities, such as Mumbai, Salem, Coimbatore, Modinagar, Jamshedpur, Hugli, Bhilai, etc. Transport Cities They may be ports primarily engaged in export and import activities such as Kandla, Cochin, Kozhikode, Vishakhapatnam, etc., or hubs of inland transport, such as Agra, Dhulia, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Nagar, Itarsi, Katni, etc. Commercial towns Towns and cities specialising in trade and commerce are kept in this class. Kolkata, Saharanpur, Satna, etc., are some examples. Mining towns These towns have developed in mineral rich areas such as Raniganj, Jharia, Digboi, Ankaleshwar, Singrauli, etc. Garrisson Cantonment towns These towns emerged as garrisson towns such as Ambala, Jalandhar, Mhow, Babina, Udhampur, etc.
cards.note: NCERT prints 'Garrisson'; the usual spelling is garrison.
reasons: review:"First six" of nine classes is an arbitrary split a student cannot know from the front; ask for all nine classes in one card (titles are short enough).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the last three classes in NCERT's functional classification of Indian towns and cities.
cards.back:
Educational towns
Religious and cultural towns
Tourist towns
cards.quote: Educational towns Starting as centres of education, some of the towns have grown into major campus towns, such as Roorki, Varanasi, Aligarh, Pilani, Prayagraj, etc. Religious and cultural towns Varanasi, Mathura, Amritsar, Madurai, Puri, Ajmer, Pushkar, Tirupati, Kurukshetra, Haridwar, Ujjain came to prominence due to their religious/cultural significance. Tourist towns Nainital, Mussoorie, Shimla, Pachmarhi, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Udagamandalam (Ooty), Mount Abu are some of the tourist destinations.
cards.note: NCERT prints 'Garrisson'; the usual spelling is garrison.
reasons: review:"Last three" of nine classes is an arbitrary split a student cannot know from the front; merge with the first six into one nine-item card.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Human beings thus, use land as a resource for production as well as ____ and ____.
cards.back: Human beings thus, use land as a resource for production as well as residence and recreation.
cards.quote: Human beings thus, use land as a resource for production as well as residence and recreation.
reasons: review:Intro filler, not an exam point; 'as well as ____ and ____' is open-ended (many uses of land fit), so no single right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ categories have undergone increases, while ____ have registered declines.
cards.back: Five categories have undergone increases, while four have registered declines.
cards.quote: Five categories have undergone increases, while four have registered declines.
reasons: review:Two bare number blanks (Five/four) cannot be derived from the front; either order is plausible.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How much scope does India have for bringing additional land under net sown area?
cards.back:
Limited
It is clear from the above discussion that the scope for bringing in additional land under net sown area in India is limited.
cards.quote: It is clear from the above discussion that the scope for bringing in additional land under net sown area in India is limited.
reasons: review:'Limited' has obvious synonyms (little, small, not much); an open 'how much' front does not force NCERT's word

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: There is, thus, an urgent need to evolve and adopt ____ technologies.
cards.back: There is, thus, an urgent need to evolve and adopt land-saving technologies.
cards.quote: There is, thus, an urgent need to evolve and adopt land-saving technologies.
reasons: review:'adopt ____ technologies' could be filled with new/modern; land-saving is only recoverable by memory, not from the front.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which temperate and subtropical crops are cultivated in the rabi season?
cards.back: facilitate the cultivation of temperate and subtropical crops such as wheat, gram and mustard.
cards.quote: facilitate the cultivation of temperate and subtropical crops such as wheat, gram and mustard.
cards.note: Low temperature in the rabi season favours these crops.
reasons: review:Back is an incomplete sentence starting at 'facilitate' (subject 'The low temperature conditions during this season' dropped); quote/back must be the full NCERT sentence.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The cultivation of ____, ____, vegetables and fodder crops during this season is done on irrigated lands.
cards.back: The cultivation of watermelons, cucumbers, vegetables and fodder crops during this season is done on irrigated lands.
cards.quote: The cultivation of watermelons, cucumbers, vegetables and fodder crops during this season is done on irrigated lands.
reasons: review:Watermelon/cucumber are trivia; 'cultivation of ____, ____, vegetables...' has many right fills (the table says vegetables, fruits, fodder).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Protective irrigation supplements rainfall. What is the strategy of this kind of irrigation?
cards.back: The strategy of this kind of irrigation is to provide soil moisture to maximum possible area.
cards.quote: The strategy of this kind of irrigation is to provide soil moisture to maximum possible area.
reasons: review:Front adds paraphrase ('supplements rainfall') not in the quoted sentence and never says what protective irrigation is; NCERT's objective sentence is missing. Definition-level, should be must.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is the yield level of rice high?
cards.back: The yield level of rice is high in Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal and Kerala.
cards.quote: The yield level of rice is high in Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal and Kerala.
reasons: review:Seven-state list of high-yield states is low-value memory load and not a distinguishing exam fact.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states are not traditional rice growing areas but now grow irrigated rice?
cards.back: Punjab and Haryana are not traditional rice growing areas.
cards.quote: Punjab and Haryana are not traditional rice growing areas.
reasons: review:Front adds 'but now grow irrigated rice', which the quoted sentence does not say; the Green Revolution 1970s fact it hints at is on the next sentence.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Maize is a food as well as ____ crop grown under semi-arid climatic conditions and over ____.
cards.back: Maize is a food as well as fodder crop grown under semi-arid climatic conditions and over inferior soils.
cards.quote: Maize is a food as well as fodder crop grown under semi-arid climatic conditions and over inferior soils.
reasons: review:Second blank 'over ____' is open-ended (inferior soils is a recall fill, not unique).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which are the leading maize producing states?
cards.back: The leading producers of maize are the states of Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
cards.quote: The leading producers of maize are the states of Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
reasons: review:Seven-state producer list is low-value memory load.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The oilseeds are produced for extracting ____.
cards.back: The oilseeds are produced for extracting edible oils.
cards.quote: The oilseeds are produced for extracting edible oils.
reasons: review:'Oilseeds are produced for extracting edible oils' is self-evident, not exam-worthy.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The HYV, fertiliser and irrigation strategy of agricultural development made India what in foodgrain production?
cards.back:
Self-reliant
This strategy of agricultural development made the country self-reliant in foodgrain production.
cards.quote: This strategy of agricultural development made the country self-reliant in foodgrain production.
reasons: review:'made India what' invites 'self-sufficient' as an equally right answer; front paraphrases 'this strategy' and the fill word is not unique

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the Farmer's Portal of India?
cards.back: The Farmer's Portal is a platform for farmers to seek any information related to agriculture.
cards.quote: The Farmer's Portal is a platform for farmers to seek any information related to agriculture.
reasons: review:Farmer's Portal is an info box with a web source; not an exam-grade definition.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Furthermore, in India, the land holdings are mostly ____.
cards.back: Furthermore, in India, the land holdings are mostly fragmented.
cards.quote: Furthermore, in India, the land holdings are mostly fragmented.

source.section: Small Farm Size and Fragmentation of Landholdings

reasons: review:'land holdings are mostly ____' also fits 'small'; fragmented is not unique from the front.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The small size fragmented landholdings are ____.
cards.back: The small size fragmented landholdings are uneconomic.
cards.quote: The small size fragmented landholdings are uneconomic.

source.section: Small Farm Size and Fragmentation of Landholdings

reasons: review:Fill could be uneconomic/unproductive/inefficient; single-word fill not unique.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Water is a ____ resource with abundant supplies on the globe.
cards.back: Water is a cyclic resource with abundant supplies on the globe.
cards.quote: Water is a cyclic resource with abundant supplies on the globe.
reasons: review:Blank has several fits: NCERT itself says 'cyclic' here but 'recyclable' on p51; 'renewable' is also a natural fill. Water's resource type is tested directly by exercise Q1(i); should be must.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In fact, a ____ proportion of freshwater is effectively available for human use.
cards.back: In fact, a very small proportion of freshwater is effectively available for human use.
cards.quote: In fact, a very small proportion of freshwater is effectively available for human use.
reasons: review:Blank 'very small' has obvious synonyms (small, tiny); not a mark-carrying single term; idea already on the 3 per cent card.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Water flow in a river depends on size of its ____ or river basin and rainfall within its catchment area.
cards.back: Water flow in a river depends on size of its catchment area or river basin and rainfall within its catchment area.
cards.quote: Water flow in a river depends on size of its catchment area or river basin and rainfall within its catchment area.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which has higher agricultural productivity: irrigated land or unirrigated land?
cards.back: irrigated lands have higher agricultural productivity than unirrigated land.
cards.quote: It has also been found that irrigated lands have higher agricultural productivity than unirrigated land.
reasons: review:Binary irrigated-vs-unirrigated question answered by common sense; no mark-carrying fact to memorise.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Further, the high yielding varieties of crops need ____, which is made possible only by a developed irrigation systems.
cards.back: Further, the high yielding varieties of crops need regular moisture supply, which is made possible only by a developed irrigation systems.
cards.quote: Further, the high yielding varieties of crops need regular moisture supply, which is made possible only by a developed irrigation systems.
reasons: review:Blank 'regular moisture supply' has near-synonyms (regular water supply); no single right fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which states has the green revolution strategy largely been successful, and why does it need irrigation?
cards.back: In fact, this is why that green revolution strategy of agriculture development in the country has largely been successful in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
cards.quote: In fact, this is why that green revolution strategy of agriculture development in the country has largely been successful in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
reasons: review:Front asks 'and why does it need irrigation?' but the back only states the states; the reason is not on the card.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The over-use of groundwater resources has led to ____ in groundwater table in these states.
cards.back: The over-use of groundwater resources has led to decline in groundwater table in these states.
cards.quote: The over-use of groundwater resources has led to decline in groundwater table in these states.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Foreign matters like micro-organisms, chemicals and wastes pollute water: what do they do to its quality and use?
cards.back: deteriorate the quality of water and render it unfit for human use.
cards.quote: Such matters deteriorate the quality of water and render it unfit for human use.
reasons: review:Common-sense statement (pollution makes water unfit); front gives away the premise, nothing exam-worthy to recall.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Sometimes, these pollutants also ____ and pollute groundwater.
cards.back: Sometimes, these pollutants also seep down and pollute groundwater.
cards.quote: Sometimes, these pollutants also seep down and pollute groundwater.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many polluting industries were located along rivers and lakes in 1997?
cards.back: The result is that in 1997, 251 polluting industries were located along the rivers and lakes.
cards.quote: The result is that in 1997, 251 polluting industries were located along the rivers and lakes.
reasons: review:Dated count (251 industries in 1997) is trivia, not a concept worth memorising.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Another way through which we can improve fresh water availability is by ____.
cards.back: Another way through which we can improve fresh water availability is by recycle and reuse.
cards.quote: Another way through which we can improve fresh water availability is by recycle and reuse.
reasons: review:'Another way to improve availability' has several valid answers (rainwater harvesting, desalination); the line needs its preceding context.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How can water after bathing and washing utensils be reused in urban areas?
cards.back: Similarly, in urban areas water after bathing and washing utensils can be used for gardening.
cards.quote: Similarly, in urban areas water after bathing and washing utensils can be used for gardening.
reasons: review:Everyday example (bathing/utensil water for gardening); low exam value.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Currently, recycling of water is practised on a ____ scale.
cards.back: Currently, recycling of water is practised on a limited scale.
cards.quote: Currently, recycling of water is practised on a limited scale.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The transformation took place when a ____, settled down in the village and took up the task of watershed development.
cards.back: The transformation took place when a retired army personnel, settled down in the village and took up the task of watershed development.
cards.quote: The transformation took place when a retired army personnel, settled down in the village and took up the task of watershed development.
reasons: review:Case-story filler (who started Ralegan Siddhi); no concept to remember.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Work began with the ____ constructed in the village.
cards.back: Work began with the percolation tank constructed in the village.
cards.quote: Work began with the percolation tank constructed in the village.
reasons: review:Case-story detail (work began with the percolation tank); filler.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What was the youth group formed in Ralegan Siddhi called?
cards.back: A youth group called Tarun Mandal was formed.
cards.quote: A youth group called Tarun Mandal was formed.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Open grazing was completely banned with a new emphasis on ____.
cards.back: Open grazing was completely banned with a new emphasis on stall-feeding.
cards.quote: Open grazing was completely banned with a new emphasis on stall-feeding.
reasons: review:Case-story detail (stall-feeding in Ralegan Siddhi); filler.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: A system of ____ (informal courts) were also set up.
cards.back: A system of Nyay Panchayats (informal courts) were also set up.
cards.quote: A system of Nyay Panchayats (informal courts) were also set up.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Watershed development in India: in majority of cases, which stage is the programme still in?
cards.back: In majority of cases, the programme is still in its nascent stage.
cards.quote: In majority of cases, the programme is still in its nascent stage.
reasons: review:Status remark about watershed programmes (time-bound, trivia); "which stage" has synonyms (early, initial, beginning) so only "nascent" is right.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Harvesting rainwater also ____ the community dependence on groundwater for domestic use.
cards.back: Harvesting rainwater also decreases the community dependence on groundwater for domestic use.
cards.quote: Harvesting rainwater also decreases the community dependence on groundwater for domestic use.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Besides the usual measures, which remedies can help solve India's water problem?
cards.back: Apart from the above mentioned factors, the issue desalinisation of water particularly in coastal areas and brackish water in arid and semi-arid areas, transfer of water from water surplus areas to water deficit areas through inter-linking of rivers can be important remedies for solving water problem in India
cards.quote: Apart from the above mentioned factors, the issue desalinisation of water particularly in coastal areas and brackish water in arid and semi-arid areas, transfer of water from water surplus areas to water deficit areas through inter-linking of rivers can be important remedies for solving water problem in India
reasons: review:Front is vague ('besides the usual measures'); several remedies are in the chapter (pricing, rainwater harvesting), so the expected answer is not fixed.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: For individual users, households and communities, what is the most important issue about water?
cards.back: the most important issue from the point of view of individual users, household and communities is pricing of water.
cards.quote: However, the most important issue from the point of view of individual users, household and communities is pricing of water.
reasons: review:Front does not constrain the answer: availability, scarcity, quality or cost are all plausible; only NCERT closing line says pricing.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Jal Kranti Abhiyan: how large a model command area is to be identified?
cards.back: Identification of model command area of about 1000 hectares in different parts of the country
cards.quote: Identification of model command area of about 1000 hectares in different parts of the country

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why must minerals be conserved and not misused, according to NCERT?
cards.back: they have to be conserved and not misused as they do not have the second crop.
cards.quote: Thus, they have to be conserved and not misused as they do not have the second crop.
reasons: review:"Why conserve minerals" has several valid answers (exhaustible, slow to form, cannot be replenished); the idiom "no second crop" cannot be derived from the front.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Most of the metallic minerals in India occur in the ____ region in the ____.
cards.back: Most of the metallic minerals in India occur in the peninsular plateau region in the old crystalline rocks.
cards.quote: Most of the metallic minerals in India occur in the peninsular plateau region in the old crystalline rocks.
reasons: review:Second blank is open: intro says metamorphic and igneous rocks, so "old crystalline rocks" is not the only valid fill.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three broad belts in which minerals are generally concentrated in India.
cards.back:
North-Eastern Plateau, South-Western Plateau and North-Western regions
Minerals are generally concentrated in three broad belts in India.
cards.quote: Minerals are generally concentrated in three broad belts in India.
reasons: review:Back first line is a composed paraphrase, not NCERT fragments (NCERT headings are "The North-Eastern Plateau Region", "The South-Western Plateau Region", "The North-Western Region"); quote does not contain the answer; should be a list card with exact headings.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Mineral belts of India: the South-Western Plateau Region is rich in which two minerals?
cards.back: This belt is rich in ferrous metals and bauxite.
cards.quote: This belt is rich in ferrous metals and bauxite.
reasons: review:"Which two minerals" is not unique: NCERT also lists high grade iron ore, manganese and limestone for this belt; "ferrous metals" is a class not a mineral; bauxite is also in the NE belt.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Ferrous minerals such as iron ore, manganese, chromite, etc., provide a strong base for the development of ____.
cards.back: Ferrous minerals such as iron ore, manganese, chromite, etc., provide a strong base for the development of metallurgical industries.
cards.quote: Ferrous minerals such as iron ore, manganese, chromite, etc., provide a strong base for the development of metallurgical industries.
reasons: review:Blank "metallurgical industries" has plausible alternatives (iron and steel industries); wording not derivable from the line.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the important iron ore mines of Odisha.
cards.back: The important mines are Gurumahisani, Sulaipet, Badampahar (Mayurbhaj), Kiruburu (Kendujhar) and Bonai (Sundergarh).
cards.quote: The important mines are Gurumahisani, Sulaipet, Badampahar (Mayurbhaj), Kiruburu (Kendujhar) and Bonai (Sundergarh).
reasons: review:List of five mine names in Odisha is detail/trivia; low recall value for CUET.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where do iron ore deposits occur in Karnataka?
cards.back: In Karnataka, iron ore deposits occur in Sandur-Hospet area of Ballari district, Baba Budan hills and Kudremukh in Chikkamagaluru district
cards.quote: In Karnataka, iron ore deposits occur in Sandur-Hospet area of Ballari district, Baba Budan hills and Kudremukh in Chikkamagaluru district
reasons: review:District-level list of Karnataka deposits is detail/trivia. Back is cut mid-list (omits Shivamogga, Chitradurg, Tumakuru from the same NCERT sentence), so the answer to "where" is incomplete.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which districts of Maharashtra is manganese mined?
cards.back: Maharashtra is also an important producer of manganese, which is mined in Nagpur, Bhandara and Ratnagiri districts.
cards.quote: Maharashtra is also an important producer of manganese, which is mined in Nagpur, Bhandara and Ratnagiri districts.
reasons: review:Districts of Maharashtra where manganese is mined is low-value detail.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which other river valleys are associated with coal?
cards.back: The other river valleys associated with coal are Godavari, Mahanadi and Sone.
cards.quote: The other river valleys associated with coal are Godavari, Mahanadi and Sone.
reasons: review:"Which other river valleys" does not say other than what; the preceding Damodar Valley context is missing from the front.

cards.subject: geography
cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

cards.subject: geography
cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

cards.subject: geography

industrial wastes

poisonous gases
chemical residuals
numerous heavy metals
dust
smoke

cards.subject: geography
cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

cards.subject: geography

Toxic gases
With increasing use of varieties of fuels as the source of energy, there is a marked increase in emission of toxic gases into the atmosphere resulting in the pollution of air.

cards.subject: geography
cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
cards.unit: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

Technological innovations
This matter has become a serious concern only in recent years due to a variety of technological innovations.

cards.subject: geography
cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

cards.subject: geography

consequent poor sanitary conditions and foul air

cards.subject: geography
cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

cards.back: The untreated wastewater of Daurala industries was leaching to the groundwater table.
cards.quote: The groundwater of this village was contaminated with heavy metals. The reason was that the untreated wastewater of Daurala industries was leaching to the groundwater table.
reasons: review:Case-story detail (Daurala); filler rather than examinable concept.

cards.subject: geography
cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
cards.unit: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
cards.front: Daurala case study: name the measures taken to restore the ecology.
cards.back:
The overhead water tank's capacity in the village was enhanced
a 900m extra pipeline was laid to supply potable water to the community
The silted pond of the village was cleaned and recharged by desilting it
Rainwater harvesting structures have been constructed at different places
1000 trees have also been planted
cards.quote: The overhead water tank's capacity in the village was enhanced and a 900m extra pipeline was laid to supply potable water to the community. The silted pond of the village was cleaned and recharged by desilting it. Large quantity of silt was removed paving way to large quantity of water so that it recharged the aquifers. Rainwater harvesting structures have been constructed at different places which has helped in diluting the contaminants of the groundwater after the monsoons. 1000 trees have also been planted which have improved the environment.
reasons: review:Case-story list (Daurala measures: tank, pipeline, pond, trees); filler.

cards.subject: geography

cards.unit: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
cards.front: What share of the world's population lives in cities at present, and what is the estimate for 2050?

reasons: review:Time-bound statistic (55%, 68% by 2050), two-part answer; not a stable fact and 'must' is too high.

reasons: review:NCERT sentence is garbled ('around 60 per cent ... attributed and about 29 per cent'); front could be answered 60 or 29; time-bound statistic.

Soil erosion
waterlogging
salinisation
alkalinisation of land

cards.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
cards.unit: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

natural
created by human beings

Stall feeding
